S58.01.needs: a Free account or a paid account
S58.01.note: The path from the first screen to Settings was not traced; only the Settings nav entry was found. Workspace-level servers are under S58.15.
steps: Sign in, open Settings, then open Connectors.
Look at the connector list. Check the Connected tab.
Compare with Expected: the connectors configured for the account appear in the list, and the Connected tab shows the ones linked to it.
S58.01.where: Settings > Connectors (tabs All, Connected, Not connected)

S58.03.note: The submit button text was not read; the mutation is in AddCustomConnectorForm in SettingsModal.tsx.
steps: Open Settings, then Connectors.
Click Add, then Add custom connector.
Type a name in My connector and a remote MCP server URL in Remote MCP server URL, then click Add connector.
Look for the new server in the Connectors list, and ask the assistant to use one of its tools.
S58.03.where: Settings > Connectors > Add > Add custom connector

labels.text: Sent only to this MCP server and never shown again.

S58.06.needs: a remote MCP server that uses a token or OAuth
S58.06.note: No explicit OAuth sign-in button text was found in this form; the Bearer token field label was not captured. Secure storage is not visible from the UI.
steps: Open Add custom connector as in S58.03.
Fill the required fields. Look at the Bearer token field if it is shown.
Click Advanced settings to show OAuth Client ID and OAuth Client Secret.
Check the help text: Sent only to this MCP server and never shown again. Compare with Expected.
S58.06.where: Settings > Connectors > Add > Add custom connector > Advanced settings

S58.07.note: No Test connection control was found. Discovery runs on connect and shows Retry discovery on failure (ConnectorCapabilitiesPanel.tsx). Searched for Test connection, Test and Connection in connectors features.

S58.08.note: The connector detail opening step was inferred from ConnectorDetail in SettingsModal.tsx.
steps: Open Settings, then Connectors, then Connected.
Click a connected connector.
Look for the Tools group with its list of tool names.
Compare with Expected: connecting shows the tools the server offers.

S58.09.needs: a connected MCP server that offers resources
S58.09.note: Attach action is in the Resources group onSelect handler; the exact button text was not captured.
steps: Open a connected connector as in S58.08.
Look for the Resources group.
Click a resource to attach it, then compare with Expected.

S58.10.needs: a connected MCP server that offers prompts
S58.10.note: Shown only where the server offers prompts.
steps: Open a connected connector as in S58.08.
Look for the Prompts group.
Click a prompt to run it, fill its arguments if asked, then compare with Expected.

S58.11.note: Transport, server name and version appear in the same panel; no separate inspector screen was found.
steps: Open a connected connector as in S58.08.
Read the Protocol line and the Tools, Resources and Prompts groups.
Open the Compatibility section and compare with Expected.

S58.12.needs: a connected MCP server that has been used
S58.12.note: Recent calls is shown; no health indicator was found. The dialog that holds it was found in ToolPermissionsPanel.tsx but its opener was not traced.
steps: Open a connected connector as in S58.08.
Find the Recent calls section at the bottom.
Use a connector tool in chat, then reopen Recent calls and compare with Expected.
S58.12.where: Settings > Connectors > [a connected connector] > Recent calls

S58.13.note: The row label comes from the connector; the + menu opening was not confirmed in code.
steps: Open the + button in the message box.
Click Connectors.
Switch the connector row off, then on, and compare with Expected.
S58.13.where: Composer + menu > Connectors > toggle the connector row

S58.15.note: Members see the same servers but cannot change them, per the page copy.
steps: Sign in as a workspace admin and open Workspace administration.
Click MCP servers under Connectors.
Read the list under Published MCP servers and the states Published to everyone or Draft, not yet published.
Click Publish to everyone or Unpublish and compare with Expected.

S58.17.needs: a connected MCP server that ships an app
S58.17.note: No fixed menu path; depends on the server offering an app tool.
steps: Send a message that asks the assistant to use a connected server's app tool.
Look for an interactive panel inside the reply.
Compare with Expected: the app panel renders in the chat.
S58.17.where: Chat > a message where a connected server's app tool runs

S58.18.needs: a connected MCP server that ships an app
S58.18.note: Handshake happens inside the embedded app panel; its effect is seen only when the app panel loads in chat (S58.17).

S58.19.needs: a connected MCP server that ships an app
S58.19.note: Host passes input, result and theme to the widget; visible only as the panel showing its content (S58.17).

S58.20.needs: a connected MCP server that ships an app and asks for an action
S58.20.note: The approval prompts were found in McpAppCard.tsx; the tool-call approval path was not traced separately.
steps: Open an app panel in chat as in S58.17.
When the app asks for a device or tool action, read the prompt.
Click Allow once or Deny and compare with Expected.
S58.20.where: Chat > app panel > Allow once / Deny prompt

S58.21.needs: a connected MCP server that ships an app
S58.21.note: Height changes show as the panel resizing inside the chat (S58.17).

S58.22.needs: a connected MCP server that ships an app
S58.22.note: Credentials are handled by the host; no control in the UI. Only the result of using the app is visible.

S58.23.needs: two accounts, one that can see an app and one that cannot
S58.23.note: Authorization is enforced by the server; visible only as the app loading or refusing for a given account.

S58.28.needs: a connected MCP server with a partial or older protocol
S58.28.note: The mismatch text appears only when the server reports a problem; the exact messages are built from the protocol data.
steps: Open a connected connector as in S58.08.
Open the Compatibility section.
Read the Unavailable during discovery line if shown, and compare with Expected.
